args.title: checkout-api: rolled back v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 in all production regions after failed health checks
args.summary: checkout-api (v2.3.1) was failing health checks in production with an elevated error rate (~18%) across all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). ROLLED BACK to v2.3.0 — the most recent release previously verified healthy in production (release history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy). Rollback completed and verified across all three production regions; current version is v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west. Note: v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so any future re-deploy of it requires change-manager approval. Action needed: confirm error rates have recovered to baseline and root-cause the v2.3.1 failures before reattempting.

trace.final:
Done.

**What I found**
- `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting `healthy: false` with an error rate of ~18%.
- Release history: v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy). Note that `v2.3.1-rc` was healthy only in **staging**, so it was not a valid production rollback target.

**What I did**
1. **Rolled back** `checkout-api` to **v2.3.0** — the most recent release verified healthy in production — across all production regions. Rollout verified; all three regions now report v2.3.0.
2. **Opened incident INC-0001 (SEV2)** for checkout-api, summarizing the failure signature and the rollback performed. On-call has been paged.

**Follow-ups worth noting**
- v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so re-deploying it (or any version in that state) requires change-manager approval under policy.
- Root cause of the v2.3.1 health-check failures is still unknown; worth investigating before any reattempt.
